prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1053; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a low-speed collision in a parking lot and stated they felt neck pain within the hour, and the file was opened for a bodily injury and property damage review.
Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene show damage to the rear bumper and tail lamp assembly, and the vehicle damage matches the impact described by the claimant.
Entry 3: The police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision, and the responding officer's notes match the location and sequence given.
Entry 4: No independent witnesses have come forward, so the file relies on scene photos, the police report, and the claimant's own statements.
Entry 5: The claimant was reached by phone and gave the same account of how the collision happened as in the initial report, with no changes in the sequence or the parties involved.
Entry 6: The driver is named on the policy and the coverage was active on the date of loss, and nothing in the records suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.
Entry 7: A check of the vehicle's prior claims and repair history shows no earlier damage to the same areas of the vehicle.
Entry 8: The claimant's medical records show a diagnosis of whiplash consistent with the kind and force of a rear-end impact, and the treatment plan followed a typical course of care.
Entry 9: Records also show no prior neck or upper back complaints or treatment, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known.
Entry 10: Follow-up notes show the claimant's symptoms improved steadily, and the frequency of visits tapered as recovery progressed.
Entry 11: Based on the medical records, vehicle damage, and police report, the claim is consistent with the reported loss and the file is moving toward a settlement evaluation.
